scenes.tts: One factor can keep a neuron alive. How can the same factor kill another cell?
scenes.visual: Title card: One Neuron, One Target. Two cultured neurons side by side, one healthy, one shrunken. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: One factor can keep a neuron alive. How can the same factor kill another cell?

scenes.tts: The last lesson left a rule. A target makes a limited amount of a survival factor. Neurons that fail to get enough die.
scenes.visual: Recap card: a target tissue releasing a few factor dots; several axons reach for them, and those that miss out fade.
scenes.narration: The last lesson left a rule. A target makes a limited amount of a survival factor. Neurons that fail to get enough die.

scenes.tts: Now picture one sympathetic neuron, in a cluster of nerve cell bodies in the neck.
scenes.visual: Zoom into the neck: a ganglion labeled superior cervical ganglion. One neuron highlighted.
scenes.narration: Now picture one sympathetic neuron, in a cluster of nerve cell bodies in the neck.

scenes.tts: Its axon runs out to a target, such as a blood vessel or a gland.
scenes.visual: The highlighted axon grows out to a blood vessel.
scenes.narration: Its axon runs out to a target, such as a blood vessel or a gland.

scenes.tts: The target makes only a small amount of nerve growth factor, N G F.
scenes.caption: The target makes only a small amount of nerve growth factor, NGF.
scenes.visual: A few NGF dimers drift off the vessel wall. Label: nerve growth factor (NGF).
scenes.narration: The target makes only a small amount of nerve growth factor, NGF.

scenes.tts: N G F is one of four mammalian neurotrophins.
scenes.caption: NGF is one of four mammalian neurotrophins.
scenes.visual: Four protein icons appear one at a time.
scenes.narration: NGF is one of four mammalian neurotrophins.

scenes.tts: N G F. Brain derived neurotrophic factor, or B D N F. Neurotrophin three. And neurotrophin four.
scenes.caption: NGF. Brain-derived neurotrophic factor, or BDNF. Neurotrophin three. And neurotrophin four.
scenes.visual: Labels fill in under the icons: NGF, BDNF, NT-3, NT-4.
scenes.narration: NGF. Brain-derived neurotrophic factor, or BDNF. Neurotrophin three. And neurotrophin four.

scenes.tts: Each is a dimer, two identical chains held together. All four share one fold.
scenes.visual: Each icon splits into two matching chains, then rejoins. Label: dimer.
scenes.narration: Each is a dimer, two identical chains held together. All four share one fold.

scenes.tts: A neuron reads them with two kinds of receptor.
scenes.visual: The axon tip enlarges; two receptor shapes sit on its membrane.
scenes.narration: A neuron reads them with two kinds of receptor.

scenes.tts: First, three Track receptors. Track A, Track B and Track C.
scenes.caption: First, three Trk receptors. TrkA, TrkB and TrkC.
scenes.visual: Three kinase-shaped receptors labeled TrkA, TrkB, TrkC. Pronunciation note on screen: Trk, said track.
scenes.narration: First, three Trk receptors. TrkA, TrkB and TrkC.

scenes.tts: Each is a receptor tyrosine kinase, and each prefers particular factors. Chapter two matches them up.
scenes.visual: A kinase domain glows inside each receptor.
scenes.narration: Each is a receptor tyrosine kinase, and each prefers particular factors. Chapter two matches them up.

scenes.tts: Second, one shared receptor, p seventy five. It binds all four factors, and it has no kinase.
scenes.caption: Second, one shared receptor, p75. It binds all four factors, and it has no kinase.
scenes.visual: A tall stalk receptor labeled p75. All four factor icons can dock on it. No kinase domain inside.
scenes.narration: Second, one shared receptor, p75. It binds all four factors, and it has no kinase.

scenes.tts: p seventy five is a relative of Fas, the death receptor you have met.
scenes.caption: p75 is a relative of Fas, the death receptor you have met.
scenes.visual: A faded Fas receptor appears beside p75, linked by a family bracket.
scenes.narration: p75 is a relative of Fas, the death receptor you have met.

scenes.tts: Like Fas, it carries a death domain. That is a stretch inside the cell that can bind proteins leading toward apoptosis.
scenes.visual: Inside the cell, a segment of p75 highlights. Label: death domain.
scenes.narration: Like Fas, it carries a death domain. That is a stretch inside the cell that can bind proteins leading toward apoptosis.

scenes.tts: But it does not use the same proteins Fas uses.
scenes.visual: Partner proteins under Fas and under p75 drawn as different shapes.
scenes.narration: But it does not use the same proteins Fas uses.

scenes.tts: What p seventy five does depends on its partners. With a partner called sortilin, it can kill.
scenes.caption: What p75 does depends on its partners. With a partner called sortilin, it can kill.
scenes.visual: A sortilin shape joins p75. A small skull icon appears beside them.
scenes.narration: What p75 does depends on its partners. With a partner called sortilin, it can kill.

scenes.tts: N G F is made first as a longer precursor, pro N G F. Its extra front stretch is the pro domain.
scenes.caption: NGF is made first as a longer precursor, proNGF. Its extra front stretch is the pro-domain.
scenes.visual: NGF drawn with an extra tail at its front. Labels: proNGF; pro-domain.
scenes.narration: NGF is made first as a longer precursor, proNGF. Its extra front stretch is the pro-domain.

scenes.tts: Enzymes cut the pro domain off to leave mature N G F. Sortilin grips the pro domain.
scenes.caption: Enzymes cut the pro-domain off to leave mature NGF. Sortilin grips the pro-domain.
scenes.visual: Scissors snip the tail off, leaving mature NGF. A sortilin shape grips a second, uncut tail.
scenes.narration: Enzymes cut the pro-domain off to leave mature NGF. Sortilin grips the pro-domain.

scenes.tts: p seventy five with sortilin binds the uncut precursor tightly.
scenes.caption: p75 with sortilin binds the uncut precursor tightly.
scenes.visual: proNGF clamped between sortilin (on the pro-domain) and p75 (on the mature part); mature NGF on p75 alone shown as a weaker, lower-affinity contact.
scenes.narration: p75 with sortilin binds the uncut precursor tightly.

scenes.tts: Two puzzles follow. First, how does a neuron know which factor is its own?
scenes.visual: Puzzle 1 on screen: Which factor is mine?
scenes.narration: Two puzzles follow. First, how does a neuron know which factor is its own?

scenes.tts: Second, add mature N G F to cultured sympathetic neurons, and they survive.
scenes.caption: Second, add mature NGF to cultured sympathetic neurons, and they survive.
scenes.visual: A culture dish; mature NGF added; neurons stay healthy.
scenes.narration: Second, add mature NGF to cultured sympathetic neurons, and they survive.

scenes.tts: Add the same protein before its pro domain has been cut off. In Barbara Hempstead's 2001 experiments, the neurons died.
scenes.caption: Add the same protein before its pro-domain has been cut off. In Barbara Hempstead's 2001 experiments, the neurons died.
scenes.visual: A second dish; uncut proNGF added; neurons shrink and break apart. On screen: Hempstead, 2001.
scenes.narration: Add the same protein before its pro-domain has been cut off. In Barbara Hempstead's 2001 experiments, the neurons died.

scenes.tts: Same protein family, opposite fates. Where would you look for the difference?
scenes.visual: The two dishes side by side. Question on screen: where is the difference?
scenes.narration: Same protein family, opposite fates. Where would you look for the difference?

scenes.tts: Look at the receptors that read it.
scenes.visual: Camera moves from the dishes to the receptors on one axon tip.
scenes.narration: Look at the receptors that read it.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea to carry through this lesson. The target supplies the factor. The neuron's receptors decide what it means.
scenes.visual: Rule card, first line: The target supplies the factor; the neuron's receptors decide what it means.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea to carry through this lesson. The target supplies the factor. The neuron's receptors decide what it means.

scenes.tts: A Track receptor reads a neurotrophin as stay alive. p seventy five can read it as die, and with sortilin it reads the uncut precursor that way.
scenes.caption: A Trk receptor reads a neurotrophin as stay alive. p75 can read it as die, and with sortilin it reads the uncut precursor that way.
scenes.visual: Rule card continues: Trk reads stay alive. p75 can read die; with sortilin, it reads the uncut precursor that way.
scenes.narration: A Trk receptor reads a neurotrophin as stay alive. p75 can read it as die, and with sortilin it reads the uncut precursor that way.

scenes.tts: Cutting the precursor removes the stretch sortilin grips. So the cut changes which receptors the factor works through best.
scenes.visual: Rule card ends: the cut removes the stretch sortilin grips, changing which receptors the factor works through best.
scenes.narration: Cutting the precursor removes the stretch sortilin grips. So the cut changes which receptors the factor works through best.

scenes.tts: How much uncut precursor reaches neurons in a normal embryo is still unsettled.
scenes.visual: Scope note: precursor in the normal embryo, unsettled.
scenes.narration: How much uncut precursor reaches neurons in a normal embryo is still unsettled.

scenes.tts: So the takeaway: the factor comes from the target, but its meaning comes from the receptors.
scenes.visual: Takeaway on screen: the factor comes from the target; its meaning comes from the receptors.
scenes.narration: So the takeaway: the factor comes from the target, but its meaning comes from the receptors.
